title: Advanced Number Properties
tagline: Year 3 — Divisor counts and sums, co-primes, perfect squares and prime-factor reasoning

introduction.overview: Year 1 and 2 used divisibility rules and HCF and LCM. Year 3 uses the prime factorisation of a number as a complete description of it. From the factorisation N = p^a × q^b × r^c you can count the divisors, add them, count the odd and even divisors, count the perfect-square or perfect-cube divisors, and count the numbers below N that are co-prime to it. These results turn long listing problems into one-line calculations.
introduction.placementRelevance: Number-property questions are commonly asked in company aptitude rounds in the harder quantitative sections, often as "how many factors" or "how many numbers up to N are co-prime to N".
introduction.realWorldContext: Gear teeth and cycle lengths (LCM and HCF), cryptographic keys (products of two large primes) and scheduling problems are built on the same factor structure.

learningObjectives: Write a number in prime-factor form and use it for counting
Count and add divisors, including odd, even, square and cube divisors
Use Euler's totient to count numbers co-prime to N
Solve HCF-LCM pair problems using prime exponents

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Every integer greater than 1 is a product of primes in exactly one way (apart from order). Two numbers are co-prime when their HCF is 1.

coreDefinitions: Prime factorisation: N = p₁^a₁ × p₂^a₂ × … × pₖ^aₖ with distinct primes pᵢ.
Number of divisors τ(N) = (a₁ + 1)(a₂ + 1)…(aₖ + 1). Sum of divisors σ(N) = Π (pᵢ^(aᵢ+1) − 1)/(pᵢ − 1).
Euler's totient φ(N): the count of integers from 1 to N that are co-prime to N; φ(N) = N × Π (1 − 1/pᵢ).
Perfect number: a number equal to the sum of its proper divisors (6, 28, 496).
A number has an odd count of divisors exactly when it is a perfect square.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: A divisor of N is built by choosing, for each prime, how many copies (from 0 up to its exponent) to use. Counting divisors is therefore counting independent choices, which is why the counts multiply.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Factorise once, write the exponents in a row, and read off every count: add 1 to each exponent and multiply for the divisor count; keep only even exponent choices for squares; drop the prime 2 for odd divisors.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Odd and even divisors
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Odd = divisors of the odd part;  Even = total − odd

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: HCF-LCM pairs
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: If HCF = h and LCM = l then a = hx, b = hy with x, y co-prime and xy = l/h

mainNarrative: Factorise first. 360 = 2³ × 3² × 5. The divisor count is (3 + 1)(2 + 1)(1 + 1) = 24 and the divisor sum is (2⁴ − 1)/1 × (3³ − 1)/2 × (5² − 1)/4 = 15 × 13 × 6 = 1170.
For odd and even divisors, remove the factor 2. The odd part of 72 = 2³ × 3² is 9, which has 3 divisors, so 72 has 3 odd divisors and 12 − 3 = 9 even ones.

Perfect-square divisors need every exponent even. In 360 = 2³·3²·5 the exponent choices that stay even are 0 or 2 for the prime 2, 0 or 2 for 3 and only 0 for 5, giving 2 × 2 × 1 = 4 square divisors (1, 4, 9, 36). Perfect-cube divisors need exponents that are multiples of 3.
To count integers up to N that are co-prime to N use φ. For N = 36 = 2²·3², φ = 36 × (1/2) × (2/3) = 12. For N = 30, φ = 30 × (1/2)(2/3)(4/5) = 8.

For pairs with given HCF h and LCM l, write the numbers as hx and hy with x and y co-prime and xy = l/h. For HCF 6 and LCM 36, xy = 6, so (x, y) is (1, 6), (6, 1), (2, 3) or (3, 2): four ordered pairs.

deepDiveAspects.title: Pairs of divisors
deepDiveAspects.content: Divisors come in pairs (d, N/d). If N has τ divisors, N can be written as a product of two factors in τ/2 ways (τ/2 + ½ if N is a square, counting the pair d = N/d once).

deepDiveAspects.title: Product of all divisors
deepDiveAspects.content: The product of all divisors of N is N^(τ/2). For N = 36 (τ = 9) it is 36^4.5 = 6⁹ = 10,077,696.

solvedExamples.title: Divisor count and sum
solvedExamples.question: Find the number of divisors and the sum of divisors of 360.
solvedExamples.conceptOrFormula: τ and σ from the exponents.
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: Each divisor is a choice of exponents.
solvedExamples.commonTrap: Forgetting to add 1 to each exponent.

solvedExamples.title: Co-primes
solvedExamples.question: How many positive integers less than 30 are co-prime to 30?
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: Numbers sharing no prime factor with 30 are 1, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19, 23, 29.

solvedExamples.title: HCF-LCM pairs
solvedExamples.question: How many ordered pairs of positive integers have HCF 6 and LCM 36?
solvedExamples.conceptOrFormula: a = 6x, b = 6y, xy = 6, x and y co-prime.
solvedExamples.commonTrap: Including (x, y) not co-prime, such as (1, 6) only.

shortcutMethods.title: Exponent row

traditionalVsShortcut.traditionalMethod: List all divisors and count them.
traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Write the exponents of the prime factorisation and apply the product, sum or totient formula directly.

rulesForApplication: τ: add 1 to each exponent and multiply.
φ uses only the distinct primes.

commonMistakes.mistake: Counting 1 or N wrongly in φ
commonMistakes.howToAvoid: φ counts numbers below N (for N > 1).

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: The divisor count of a non-square number is even; reject odd options.
placementTips.questionSelectionAdvice: Always factorise first and write the exponent row.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: Divisor and totient counts appear in cycle-length and remainder questions later.

easy.question: The number of divisors of 144 is
The sum of all divisors of 28 is
easy.explanation: The divisors are 1, 2, 4, 7, 14 and 28, which add to 56.

easy.question: The smallest number having exactly 6 divisors is
easy.explanation: 12 = 2² × 3 has (2 + 1)(1 + 1) = 6 divisors, and no smaller number has 6.

intermediate.question: The sum of all divisors of 360 is
The number of integers from 1 to 36 that are co-prime to 36 is
In how many ways can 360 be written as a product of two distinct positive factors (order ignored)?
intermediate.explanation: 360 has 24 divisors, which pair up into 12 pairs.

advanced.question: How many integers from 1 to 30 are co-prime to 30?
The smallest number having exactly 12 divisors is
advanced.explanation: 60 = 2² × 3 × 5 has 3 × 2 × 2 = 12 divisors; no smaller number has 12.

placementStyle.question: The largest 3-digit number having exactly 3 divisors is
placementStyle.explanation: Numbers with exactly 3 divisors are squares of primes. 31² = 961 is the largest below 1000.

placementStyle.question: The number of divisors of 2⁵ × 3³ × 5² that are perfect cubes is
placementStyle.explanation: Cube divisors need exponents that are multiples of 3: 2 has {0, 3}, 3 has {0, 3}, 5 has {0}. So 2 × 2 × 1 = 4.

placementStyle.question: The number of ordered pairs of positive integers with HCF 6 and LCM 36 is
placementStyle.explanation: Write the numbers as 6x and 6y with xy = 6 and x, y co-prime: (1, 6), (6, 1), (2, 3), (3, 2): 4.

keyTakeaways: Squares have an odd divisor count.
selfCheckQuestions: Can I count the divisors of 360?
